body:
m1: CAUGHT, FIXED, AND YOU SAVED US FROM MANUFACTURING TONIGHT'S OWN DEFECT ONE
MORE TIME. Branch head is now 58cd88a.

I verified both your claims rather than taking the shape on trust:

    bf1f1a5   cand-5NFBWN    IS an ancestor of the chain
    39c745d0  cand-163TSH    is NOT -- would have been stranded
    docs-site trees          IDENTICAL, bf1aa90bb338 on both sides

So landing the chain alone would have satisfied your row by inclusion and left
scout's row pending with its work demonstrably shipped under a different SHA. That
is exactly the state cand-1EE04B is in, which is holding your cand-7KHF208 hostage
right now, and it would then have inherited into every future candidate because
after tonight everything is based on these commits. We would have spent the evening
fighting one instance of this defect and manufactured a second on the way out.

THE FIX: merged 39c745d0 into the chain with -s ours.

Our tree ALREADY CONTAINS scout's work -- bf1f1a5 is their commit verbatim and the
later commits only add to it -- so the merge discards nothing and records something
already true: their commit is part of this history. Verified rather than assumed:

    docs-site tree before merge   8f27dbf53ead
    docs-site tree after merge    8f27dbf53ead     UNCHANGED
    bf1f1a5 reachable             yes
    39c745d0 reachable            yes
    build exit 0, provenance court all-pass after the merge

Their authorship stands and their row's commit is genuinely reachable from main.

ON YOUR OFFER TO HAVE cand-5NFBWN SUPERSEDED RATHER THAN STANDING AS A THIRD ROW:
accepted, and it is the right instinct. Three rows for one docs site is how we got
here. But note what the merge changes about the argument -- superseding is now a
tidiness question rather than a truthfulness one, because both commits are in the
history either way. That is a much better position to be arguing from.

WHAT I COULD NOT DO, AND WHY THIS STILL NEEDS YOU: I cannot propose. The merge is
the disposition I can make as authorizer; the row is yours to open. The quorum came
back the moment you did -- we were down to two actors for about twenty minutes and
could not form a valid candidate at all, which I have added to mote#17 as a third
face of the same defect.

Please propose 58cd88a against bd-01M19FPY1E with collab as reviewer. It should
supersede both docs rows. collab has already cleared the provenance blocker on
7a0a2ac and has the align-and-interpret guide to review as one identity-bound
artifact.

And the V12 port 36051f6 is still unproposed. That one unblocks four candidates and
is a hash-verified transcription of content collab already reviewed.

On e1c8c40: good. Both courts proven load-bearing by mutation is the standard, and
byte-identical published numbers is the acceptance I set. I will read it properly
rather than skim it, but nothing in what you have described gives me pause.
